easy.def: A loud sound that warns you.
examples: The fire alarm rang.
An alarm woke me.
The alarm is loud.

more.def: A loud sound or signal that warns of danger or wakes you up.
examples: The fire alarm rang in the school.
My alarm woke me at seven.
The car alarm went off.

easy.def: A book for keeping photos or stamps.
examples: I look at the photo album.
My stamp album is full.
The album has old pictures.

more.def: A book with pages for keeping photos, stamps or other things you collect.
examples: We looked through the family photo album.
She put the new stamp in her album.
The album was full of baby pictures.

easy.def: A group of songs sold together.
examples: The singer made an album.
I love this album.
The album has twelve songs.

more.def: A collection of songs that is sold together.
examples: The band released a new album this summer.
My favorite song is on the album.
The album has ten songs.

easy.def: Awake and ready to notice things.
examples: The dog is alert.
Stay alert on the trail.
The guard was alert.

more.def: Watching and ready to notice or react to what is going on.
examples: The alert deer lifted its head at the slightest sound.
Stay alert when you cross the street.
After a good night's sleep, she felt fresh and alert.
The bell alerted the class.
I alert Mom.
The alarm alerts us.

more.def: To warn someone about a danger or something important.
examples: The siren alerted people about the storm.
My barking dog alerted us to the stranger.
She alerted the teacher to the broken window.

easy.def: A creature from another planet in stories.
examples: The alien had green skin.
The movie is about an alien.
I drew an alien.

more.def: A pretend visitor from another planet in stories and movies.
examples: The alien stepped out of the spaceship.
In the movie, an alien made friends with a boy.
I drew an alien with three eyes.
It felt alien to be in a new place.
The alien land was strange.
The food seemed alien.

more.def: Strange, unfamiliar or from another place.
examples: The new city felt alien to her at first.
An alien smell filled the air.
The customs seemed alien to the visitors.
The twins look alike.
The two cats are alike.
We think alike.

more.def: Very similar, not different.
examples: The twins look so alike that few can tell them apart.
The two puppies are alike in color.
My friend and I think alike.
The fish is alive.
Plants are alive.
Is the bug still alive?

more.def: Living, and not dead.
examples: The scientists found a tiny animal that was still alive.
Plants are alive even though they do not move around.
The old tree is still alive and grows new leaves each spring.
All the kids can play.
I ate all my peas.
She read all the books.

more.def: The whole amount of something, or every one of a group.
examples: All the students lined up for the fire drill.
We stayed inside all day because of the rain.
The squirrel hid all of the acorns before winter.
The cat walked down the alley.
The alley is narrow.
We cut through the alley.

more.def: A narrow street or path between buildings.
examples: The cat slipped down the alley.
We took a shortcut through the alley behind the shop.
Trash cans lined the alley.
Mom will allow me to stay up late.
The pool does not allow running.
Dad allowed us to have one more cookie.

more.def: To give permission for someone to do or have something.
examples: The museum does not allow visitors to touch the paintings.
Our teacher allows us to read quietly after a test.
Dogs are not allowed inside the bakery.

easy.def: A friend or partner who helps you.
examples: The two countries are allies.
He was my ally in the game.
Allies help each other.

more.def: A person or country that joins with another to help.
examples: The two countries were allies in the war.
My brother was my ally when I needed help.
Bees are allies of the garden.
I am almost done.
It is almost bedtime.
We almost missed the bus.

more.def: Very nearly, but not completely.
examples: The glass was almost full, so I poured slowly.
It was almost midnight when the train arrived.
She almost won the race, but another runner passed her at the end.
I was alone.
She likes to be alone.
He played alone.

more.def: By yourself, with nobody else.
examples: The lighthouse keeper lived alone on the rocky island.
She likes to read alone in the quiet room.
He did not feel alone with his dog beside him.
I walked alone.
She did it alone.
Can you carry it alone?

more.def: Without any help or company from others.
examples: I made the whole model airplane alone.
He walked home alone after school.
Wolves often hunt together, but a bear usually hunts alone.

easy.def: Next to or following a path.
examples: We walked along the river.
Trees grow along the road.
A line of ducks swam along the shore.

more.def: Following the length of something, such as a road, river or wall.
examples: Bicycle riders pedaled along the path beside the lake.
Pretty flowers grew along the garden wall.
The train rolled slowly along the tracks.
Come along!
Bring your dog along.
Can I come along?

more.def: Together with someone else.
examples: We are going to the zoo, and you can come along.
She brought her little sister along to the swimming pool.
Can you bring a snack along for the trip?
I also like cake.
She also sings.
He is also here.

more.def: In addition, or as well as something already said.
examples: Frogs live in water, and they also live on land.
She plays the violin and also sings in the choir.
The park has swings, and there is also a pond.
Although it rained, we played.
He ran, although he was tired.
I like pie, although I am full.

more.def: In spite of the fact that; even though.
examples: Although it was cold, we went outside.
She smiled, although she was nervous.
We stayed, although the movie was long.

easy.def: All the time, or every time.
examples: I always brush my teeth.
The sun always rises.
She is always happy.

more.def: At all times, or every time, without change.
examples: The sun always rises in the east.
My grandmother always sings when she cooks.
He is always the first one to arrive at school.
